milestones.title: Guardrails: strict TS, lint rules, jest, invariant/Result, standards checker, npm run verify
milestones.note:
Covers plan M1.1–M1.7, using §4 "Standards enforcement" for the values. Pin tsx@4.23.15 and @types/node@26.6.3 as devDependencies. @types/node 26.6.3 is already in node_modules as a transitive dependency, so only package.json proves the install. Both tsconfig.json and scripts/tsconfig.json must resolve strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, noImplicitReturns, noUnusedLocals and noUnusedParameters to true, and the scripts program must include scripts/check/standards.ts. eslint.config.js needs max-lines-per-function {max: 60}, no-empty, @typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises and @typescript-eslint/switch-exhaustiveness-check at error, plus a src/domain no-restricted-imports that bans react, react-native, expo* and @/. It must also ignore .cache/, .expo/ and .claude/, because worktrees under .claude/ break typescript-eslint's projectService (roomsmith/eslint.config.js documents this). The gates rely on these contracts. src/lib/invariant.ts exports invariant and InvariantError, and src/lib/result.ts exports ok, err and isOk (gate 11 calls invariant(false) directly). The package.json jest block uses preset jest-expo/ios, with testMatch kept inside src/**/__tests__. Every node:test case in scripts/check/__tests__/standards.test.ts has its rule id in its own name or in its describe block's name: fn-length, assertions, marker, skipped-test, recursion (two cases: a self-call and a cross-file a<->b cycle), silent-catch and clean. `npx tsx scripts/check/standards.ts` run with no arguments scans the repo including src/app, exits non-zero, and prints the file path and rule id for each violation. Gate 20 proves this by writing an unasserted function to src/app/ratchet-probe-tmp.tsx for one run. Retrofit src/app/_layout.tsx and src/app/index.tsx with at least 2 invariant() calls each. npm run verify must chain tsc for the app, tsc -p scripts/tsconfig.json, eslint --max-warnings 0, the standards checker, jest and node --test. Traps: the checker must follow its own rules. It must walk the AST with an explicit stack, because a recursive visit/forEachChild is the recursion it bans. It must read TODO markers from comments and skips from call expressions, so the fixture strings in its own test file don't trip the repo scan. It must also settle how anonymous test callbacks longer than 5 lines meet the 2-assertion rule. The gates call node_modules/.bin directly because under CI=1 a bare npx quietly downloads a missing tool. lib.sh's nodetest_nonempty is a false green on Node 26: the file-level wrapper counts as a pass, so an empty test file passes. That is why gates 12–19 count the real named passes themselves.

GATE NAMING (from the gate fix pass): Gates 13-19 count only passing test leaves whose full name 'describe … it' matches the keyword (fn-length, assertions, marker, skipped-test, recursion x2, silent-catch, clean). Put each keyword in the it() name, for example it('fn-length: flags a 61-line function'), and keep describe names free of those words, because a describe titled 'clean' or 'recursion' would make every test under it match. Gate 21 finds every .tsx under src/app and needs >= 2 standalone invariant( calls in each. Every route or layout component must therefore be a named function with its own invariants (no anonymous default-export arrow). The standards checker must print violations with a path that contains src/app/ (gate 20 needs 'ratchet-probe-tmp' and 'assertions' in its output) and exit 0 only when the whole repo is clean.

Shared helpers: scripts/ratchet/lib.sh — nodetest_case matches the FULL test name (describe … leaf, case-insensitive), counts only real passing leaves (not parent test() wrappers, not the Node 26 empty-file wrapper) and forbids skip/todo; jest runs via node_modules/.bin only.

milestones.title: Our own GTFS-realtime protobuf decoder, proven against the protobufjs oracle
milestones.note:
This card covers plan tasks M1.8–M1.13 (§5, plus the §4 "GTFS-RT decoder" bullet). The builder writes wire.ts, utf8.ts, decode-feed.ts, decode-vehicle.ts and decode-trip-update.ts as pure code under src/domain/gtfsrt, with tests in __tests__. It also runs `npm i -D gtfs-realtime-bindings@2.2.0`, which is the npm latest and depends on protobufjs ^8 and long. Then it writes scripts/fixtures/make-gtfsrt-fixture.ts, which generates __fixtures__/vehicle-positions.fixture.ts. The card depends on m1a_guardrails for jest, tsx and `npm run verify`.

TEST NAMES ARE GATED. Each pattern below is a case-insensitive regex matched against the describe+it full name, and it must match at least one PASSED test:
- wire: `300`, `negative`, `float32`, `wire type 3`, `past the end`
- utf8: one test per string, named with `Gov’t Center` (curly U+2019), `Ñ`, `🚆` and `abc`, plus a test named with `FFFD`
- decode-vehicle: `timestamp`, `latitude`, `trip id`, `unknown field 1000`
- decode-trip-update: `-45`, `arrival time`, `stopId`, `SKIPPED`
- oracle: `3 vehicles`, `2 trip updates`, `uint64`, `unicode`

Traps:
- Ten-byte -1 and delay -45 are sign-extended 10-byte varints, so they need int32 `|0` truncation. Do not use 32-bit `<<` past 28 bits.
- protobufjs decodes uint64 as a Long, so compare via `toObject(m, {longs: Number})`.
- No non-test file under src/ (the fixture included) may contain the quoted string 'protobufjs' or 'gtfs-realtime-bindings'. The src/domain no-restricted-imports rule must still allow the bindings inside __tests__.
- The generator must be deterministic: fixed timestamps, no Date.now and nothing that depends on the time zone. The gate deletes the fixture, regenerates it and requires it to match byte for byte. It then re-runs under TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati and runs `git diff --exit-code` against the index, so stage or commit a fixture that was changed after an earlier commit.

For the arbiter:
- lib.sh's `jest_nonempty <path> <name>` (the -t form) fails correct builds when a file has more than one test. Jest counts tests filtered out by -t as skipped, and the helper rejects any skipped test. That is why the card uses a local `jest_cases` (an unfiltered `--json` run) in its place.
- jest is not installed yet, so jest_cases' reading of the `--json` report (`testResults[].assertionResults[].{fullName,status}`) was proven only against shimmed reports. It has not been tested against a real jest binary.
- The verify runs about 10 jest passes plus full_gate.

Shared helpers: scripts/ratchet/lib.sh — nodetest_case matches the FULL test name (describe … leaf, case-insensitive), counts only real passing leaves (not parent test() wrappers, not the Node 26 empty-file wrapper) and forbids skip/todo; jest runs via node_modules/.bin only.

milestones.title: Network model: station clustering + names, stop-pattern line derivation, shape geometry, block links, transfers, calendar
milestones.note:
This card builds plan tasks M2.9–M2.14 (§5, plus §4 pipeline steps 7–12). It depends on m1 (jest, tsx, invariant/Result, npm run verify) and on m2a, whose M2.4 mini-feed fixture the build-network and calendar tests should use. Each acceptance case must be its own passing test whose name matches its gate pattern (jest -t is case-insensitive, node:test is case-sensitive). The required names are:
- network: "Government Center N+S cluster to rail:government-ctr", "stops 808/832/841 cluster to mover:bayfront-park", and "every name is Title Case, has no STATION/METRORAIL, <= 28 chars".
- lines: exactly 15 test.each cases containing "real-pattern" (that token is reserved for those cases), "touching both branches -> Err", and "School Board -> MM_OMNI".
- shape-geometry: "cumulative distance ±1 m", "projection is monotone on a loop", and "offset > 100 m -> Err".
- build-network: "Inner Loop halves get next_trip_idx", "single-track trips get a note", "destination = last station", "same-station transfer = 60 s", "rail↔mover only within 400 m", and "transfer table is symmetric".
- calendar: names containing 1790740800, containing 1793509200, and "Labor Day 20260907 swaps the weekday service".

Trap: baseEpoch follows the GTFS noon-minus-12h rule, not local midnight, so baseEpoch(20261101) must be 1793509200 (local midnight gives 1793505600). Gates 25–26 import scripts/gtfs/calendar.ts and call an exported `baseEpoch(yyyymmdd: number): number` directly, so do not return a Result from it. Trap: §1 says a "design record" lists the 15 real patterns, but no such record is on disk (I searched ~/Documents/Repos and ~/.claude/plans on 2026-10-01). §1 also files the 15 under Metrorail, while this card says rail/mover. Take the patterns from the real feed (a public zip that needs no key) or raise a blocked_question, and never invent them. Headsigns are wrong: weekend Green trips are signed "EHT - CUL SINGLE TRACK AFTER 8PM", which is why destination must be the last station. Not yet checked: jest isn't installed, so jest_named has only been run against canned jest summaries. base_epoch_is has only been run with Node's built-in TypeScript stripping and a stand-in tsx, so the prover should re-run both once m1 lands.

GATE NAMING (from the gate fix pass): Gates match the FULL test name ('describe … test', case-insensitive, in the gate's word order). For the Mover shapes name the tests '<HEADSIGN> shape <id> derives <LINE> by stop pattern': 123745 is MM_OMNI (School Board -> Gov Ctr, 9 stops), 123746 is MM_BRICKELL (Financial District -> Gov Ctr, 13 stops), and 123748 is MM_BRICKELL. For the rail headsigns name them 'headsign "EHT - CUL SINGLE TRACK AFTER 8PM" derives GREEN by stop pattern', plus the same with '8 PM'; the build-network note tests are named 'single-track note on headsign "<each spelling>"'. Exactly 15 full jest names in src/domain/lines may contain 'real-pattern', so keep that word out of every other test and describe title there (gate 7 is an exact count).

milestones.title: Schedule DB: schema + atomic writer, verifier, manifest, deterministic build CLI, real build, derivation report
milestones.note:
Covers plan tasks M2.15–M2.20: schema.ts/write-db.ts plus scripts/lib/node-sql-executor.ts, verify-db.ts, manifest.ts, build.ts with the `gtfs:build` script, the real county build into assets/db/{schedule.db,manifest.json} (it downloads the public keyless zip), and report.ts. The values that must hold: serviceEnd.rail.date 20261122 and serviceEnd.mover.date 20261231; service-end epochs in seconds of 1795410000 (rail) and 1798779600 (Mover), under any field name inside serviceEnd.rail/.mover; these equal start(end date, America/New_York) + 86400, the same formula as M2.14 baseEpoch. Also: counts.trips > 4000 and equal to count(trip); dbBytes equal to the file size and < 6e6; dbSha256 equal to sha256(schedule.db); PRAGMA user_version 1 and integrity_check ok; all 15 §4 tables present, including trip.next_trip_idx. Traps: (a) an UNCHANGED rerun must write nothing (sha256 and mtime of both files are checked). (b) `npm run gtfs:build -- --force` must print BUILT and give back a byte-identical DB, so keep timestamps and unordered iteration out of the DB, and keep the zip in .cache/ so --force still works after a 304. (c) verify-db.ts and report.ts need a CLI main-guard, and report.ts must default to assets/db/schedule.db. (d) The node executor stays in scripts/lib, never src/: node:sqlite must not reach Metro, even though §4 says src/data. The gate is stricter than the plan's own M2.19 V command, because `m.counts.trips<4000` passes when the field is undefined and `npm run gtfs:build | grep -q UNCHANGED` can break on SIGPIPE under pipefail. §4 points to the 'full DDL in the design record', but that DDL is not in any file in the mesh (it appears only in session transcripts), so write the DDL from the §4 table list and what M3's queries need. If the county republishes the feed before this runs (risk R11; the baseline is 8,419,295 bytes, last-modified 2026-07-31), gates 10/11 will fail on the plan's dates: stop and escalate to Jamie, do not edit the gate. Authoring check 2026-10-01: `bash -n` OK; the full run exits 1 at line 15 `need_file scripts/gtfs/schema.ts` → 'ratchet: missing file scripts/gtfs/schema.ts'. Each of the 18 gates fails cleanly on its own on today's repo. Gates 6–17 were also run against a synthetic scratch repo: they pass when the build is correct and fail on each injected defect (trips=4000, dbSha256 missing, epoch in ms, a rerun that rewrites, nondeterministic --force, --force ignored, a no-op verify-db, report missing a line or exiting 1, user_version 0 or a table dropped, gtfs:build script missing).

GATE NAMING (from the gate fix pass): Gates 3–20 match each node:test case by its FULL name ("describe … test", case-insensitive), so every acceptance case must be its own passing test named in the plan's wording. The names that satisfy each pattern:
- write-db: "row counts match after reopen", "integrity_check = ok", "user_version = 1", "journal_mode is delete", "the write is an atomic rename".
- verify-db: "every trip has ≥ 2 stop times", "times are monotone", "every line is in the catalog", "size < 6 MB", "a corrupted DB -> Err naming the check".
- manifest: "has every field", "rail service-end epoch = start(end date) + 86400".
- build: "mini feed -> BUILT", "a rerun -> UNCHANGED, DB mtime unchanged", "--force gives the identical dbSha256".

The verify-db CLI must exit non-zero on a DB whose stop_time table is empty, and its output must contain "stop time", "stop_time" or "stopTime" (gate 31). The writer must leave the committed schedule.db in journal_mode delete, not WAL (gates 6 and 30).

tsx must be a devDependency in node_modules, because gates 24, 31 and 32 run it via local_bin and never download it.

Shared helpers: scripts/ratchet/lib.sh — nodetest_case matches the FULL test name (describe … leaf, case-insensitive), counts only real passing leaves (not parent test() wrappers, not the Node 26 empty-file wrapper) and forbids skip/todo; jest runs via node_modules/.bin only.

ARBITER RULING — SHAPE ENDS (2026-10-01, measured by the arbiter on the live feed; see plan 'M2.11 ruling'): the county's rail shapes stop short of the terminal platforms. Palmetto 9486/9487 lies 102.7–103.6 m PAST the shape end along the track (only 4.5–5.4 m lateral); Dadeland South 9528 ~50 m past; MIA 10494 is 76 m lateral. m2b implemented the plan's plain 'offset > 100 m -> Err', so the real build (M2.19) currently fails at Palmetto. Implement the ruling in src/domain/schedule/shape-geometry.ts (m2b's file — you may change it; ALL existing m2b tests must stay green): (1) INTERIOR stops keep nearest-on-shape <= 100 m. (2) The FIRST and LAST stop of a pattern are measured against the terminal segment extended as a ray: lateral <= 100 m AND along-track overhang past the shape end <= 150 m. (3) When a terminal stop overhangs, append its projection on the ray as the new terminal shape point, so the polyline reaches the platform and dist_m stays monotone; record the added metres in a new column shape.extended_m REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 (schema). (4) Overhang > 150 m or lateral > 100 m -> Err naming stop and shape. Add separately-named tests: 'terminal stop 103 m past the shape end on the track is accepted and the shape is extended to it', 'terminal overhang > 150 m -> Err', 'terminal lateral > 100 m -> Err'. In the real build, shapes 211239/211246/211260/211263/211270 must end with extended_m between 100 and 110; verify-db should assert every shape's extended_m <= 150.

milestones.title: Schedule engine II: scheduled vehicle positions, real-DB snapshot, expiry, schedule DB provider
milestones.note:
Builds plan tasks M3.5–M3.8. Every gate is one command per line, because under set -e a failing a && b line does not stop the script. To run one gate alone: bash -c 'source scripts/ratchet/verify-m3b_positions_provider.sh; <gate>'. The case gates match test names (describe + it, case-insensitive), so name the tests to fit:
(1) positions.test.ts needs passing tests named for "midpoint" (shape midpoint ±1 m), "before start" (none) and "layover" (a block gap of 600 s or less parks the vehicle at the next trip's first stop; the vehicle key is date:block_id).
(2) positions-real.test.ts needs passing tests matching 'Wed 08:00.*rail', 'Wed 08:00.*mover' and '50 ?m', and must query assets/db/schedule.db in place, not a copy or the mini feed. Wed 2026-09-30 08:00 America/New_York is epoch 1790769600. Count distinct vehicle keys so the chained Inner Loop half-trips are not counted twice. Measure the 50 m against the shape_point polyline independently, not through the interpolator's own projection.
(3) Expiry tests must name ok, warn, urgent, expired, rail and mover. Boundaries: 14 days → warn, 3 → urgent, 0 → urgent, below 0 → expired. Rail ends 20261122 and Mover ends 20261231, each with end = start(end date) + 86400.
M3.8 traps:
- Read the SDK 57 expo-sqlite docs. SQLiteProvider's assetSource does not overwrite a database that already has the same name, so the sha-keyed name is what makes new data land on the phone. The plan says "feed sha", but a builder-only change keeps the feed sha while the DB bytes change, so keying on the manifest's dbSha256 is safer (arbiter's call).
- Clean up old copies, including -wal/-shm files, in a bounded loop.
- Keep metro.config.js's db assetExt.
- Repoint the M1.16 data probe, which counts 1000 rows in probe.db, to the schedule DB.
- Mount the provider from a non-test module.
- Leave no 'probe.db', 'make-probe-db' or 'scripts/probe/' strings in src/, scripts/ (outside scripts/ratchet), package.json or metro.config.js.
- Gate 11 requires the iOS export to contain exactly one db asset, byte-identical to assets/db/schedule.db.
For the arbiter:
- Once this card lands, m1c's verify goes red by design. Its gates 1–2 run scripts/probe/make-probe-db.ts and need assets/db/probe.db. Do not restore the probe to make m1c green again.
- lib.sh's nodetest_nonempty passes a test file with zero tests: Node 26 prints "# pass 1" for it (I checked this in a scratch dir). That is why gate 4 uses its own helper.

milestones.title: Realtime domain: per-provider constants, GTFS-RT mapper, transports, chain + quota, poll scheduler, merges
milestones.note:
This card covers plan tasks M4.1–M4.7 (§3 values plus the §4 Live interface, merge rules and Polling). It needs M1 (jest-expo, tsx, `npm run verify`), the M1.13 fixture and M3's trip-to-pattern data, which the pure domain takes as an injected lookup. Named cases go through the script's own `jest_cases` helper instead of lib.sh, because `jest_nonempty -t` counts every filtered-out test as skipped (checked against real jest 30.5.2: "2 skipped, 1 passed"). The helper runs one file with `--json`, matches each name as a case-insensitive substring of describe plus test name, and allows no skipped or todo tests. Copy the case strings from the `jest_cases` calls exactly, and write the merge table with `it.each`. Exact values: Swiftly 30 s / fresh ≤75 / max age 150; Transitland 60/150/210; 8 s abort; backoff 15→30→60→120 with a 120 cap, and a 429 doubles the interval; fail over after 3 failures and re-probe after 300 s; Transitland skipped at ≥9500 and kept at 9499; quota resets on the 1st; greedy match ≤800 m; Swiftly header `Authorization: <key>` (no Bearer) with agencyKey default `miami`; Transitland header `apikey`; all 4 feed URLs written out in transports.test.ts; fake keys only. Traps: (1) src/live/quota.ts is outside the plan's `npx jest src/domain/live`, so gate 7 runs its test directly. (2) user.db does not exist until M7.3, so quota needs an injected store, and wiring it to user.db is a dependency-order gap with no owner yet; the arbiter must give it a home. (3) §4 rule 6 belongs to M4.7's merge-departures, not the vehicle table. (4) The 15 s first backoff is shorter than both cadences, and the plan does not say whether retries are clamped to the cadence (this matters for Transitland quota and Swiftly's 30 s cache rule). (5) The rail line cannot be told from position on the shared Green/Orange trunk, so the builder must pick a behavior, state it and test it. (6) New fixture entities (trip updates, an out-of-scope route, a vehicle with no trip_id) must come from scripts/fixtures/make-gtfsrt-fixture.ts, because m1b's gate regenerates that fixture. Run today: exit 1 at line 45 `need_file src/domain/live/types.ts` ("ratchet: missing file src/domain/live/types.ts"). Each gate also fails on its own today, and a run against stub files with correctly named tests passed all 12. Side effect while authoring: my first stub run was wrongly launched from zsh, so `npx jest` downloaded jest 30.5.2 into ~/.npm/_npx/b8d86e6551a4f492. That is outside the repo, and nothing in the repo changed except this script.

GATE NAMING (from the gate fix pass): Gates pin jest tests by case-insensitive substring of the FULL name (describe titles + test title). Name the tests so they contain the exact strings quoted in gates 2–4 and 6–12, for example 'per capability', 'never fetches trip_updates', 'transitland departures url' and 'malformed row returns Err without throwing'. Do not use it.skip or it.todo; skipped or todo tests fail the gate. The string `trip_updates` must not appear anywhere in src/domain/live/transports.ts, not even in a comment. Swiftly's hyphenated `gtfs-rt-trip-updates` is fine. transports.test.ts must also contain a concrete departures URL literal such as https://transit.land/api/v2/rest/stops/f-dhw-miamidadetransit:9513/departures?next=3600; a `${stopId}` template literal does not satisfy gate 5. jest must be a local devDependency, because jest_cases runs node_modules/.bin/jest and never npx.

Plan changed 2026-10-01 after a live probe with Jamie's Transitland key: trip_updates.pb is 1 MB/poll and is NEVER fetched; predictions come from per-station departures (task M4.3b). milestones.title: Realtime runtime: HTTP with typed errors + byte counter, Keychain keys, providers, polling hook, embedded-key guard
milestones.note:
This card covers plan M4.8–M4.10. M4.8 is src/live/http.ts on expo/fetch (abort gives {kind:'timeout'}, a rejected fetch gives 'network', a non-2xx response gives 'http' with its status, plus a byte counter) and src/live/keys.ts, which may use expo-secure-store only. M4.9 is providers/{none,swiftly,transitland}.ts, use-live-polling.ts and live-context.tsx: polling stops on AppState, and nothing under src/live may read process.env or any EXPO_PUBLIC_ name. The gates also require src/live/__tests__/http.test.ts with passing tests whose names match /timeout|abort/, /network/, /status/ and /byte/; expo/fetch is native, so either inject the fetch function or use a jest.mock labelled `// test-time mock of native module`. The guard's command-line interface is `npx tsx scripts/check/embedded-keys.ts [--dir <bundle dir, default .cache/export>] [--tree] [--self-test]`, and it must behave as follows: the secrets are the values of TRANSITLAND_API_KEY, SWIFTLY_API_KEY and any EXPO_PUBLIC_*KEY, taken from process.env and .env combined; empty values are skipped, and SWIFTLY_AGENCY_KEY=miami is not a secret ('miami' is in the bundle); an EXPO_PUBLIC_\w*KEY name in the bundle is also a hit; on a hit it exits non-zero and names the variable (and, with --tree, the file) but never prints the value; if it scans zero bundle files it must fail; --self-test prints a line containing 'self-test'. Watch for these: the real export is Hermes bytecode (.cache/export/_expo/static/js/ios/entry-*.hbc), so the guard must byte-scan every file with no *.js-only glob and no skipping of binary files; --tree must list files with `git ls-files` (the index, which respects GIT_INDEX_FILE), not HEAD; and tests must build any EXPO_PUBLIC_…KEY string at runtime, or --tree will flag their own source. The publish script must be `npm run verify && npx expo export --platform ios --output-dir .cache/export && npx tsx scripts/check/embedded-keys.ts && npx eas-cli@24.8.0 update --skip-bundler --input-dir .cache/export --channel production --environment production --platform ios --non-interactive`, chained with && only and with eas update last. Without --skip-bundler, eas-cli 24.8.0 bundles again into dist/ using the EAS server env (checked in build/commands/update/index.js), so the guard would check a bundle that is never uploaded; never run publish or eas while building. Run before the build: exit 1 at gate 1 (`ratchet: missing file src/live/http.ts`). Gates 6–17 passed in a dry run against a scratch reference guard, and each of 13 broken guard or publish variants failed at its intended gate (one more, '.env overrides process.env', cannot be caught without a .env).

GATE NAMING (from the gate fix pass): Test names: http.test.ts full test names (describe + test, case-insensitive) must contain 'timeout', 'network', 'non-2xx' and 'byte'. Non-test code under src/live must use AppState, and no file under src/live (tests included) may contain process.env or the public env prefix. Guard contract the gates rely on: read secret values from process.env, where process.env wins over .env; ignore empty values and the non-secret SWIFTLY_AGENCY_KEY; scan every file under --dir (default .cache/export), binaries included; name leaks by variable (plus the file under --tree, which lists tracked files via git so it honours GIT_INDEX_FILE) and never print a value; on success print 'scanned <N> files' with the dir; for an empty or missing dir print 'no bundle files' with the dir and exit 1 without a stack trace; --self-test prints 'self-test … pass'. The publish script must be exactly verify && expo export --platform ios --output-dir D && the guard on D && eas update --channel production --environment production --platform ios --skip-bundler --input-dir D, with eas update last.

Shared helpers: scripts/ratchet/lib.sh — nodetest_case matches the FULL test name (describe … leaf, case-insensitive), counts only real passing leaves (not parent test() wrappers, not the Node 26 empty-file wrapper) and forbids skip/todo; jest runs via node_modules/.bin only.

milestones.title: Feed operations: change check, one-command refresh, determinism on the real feed
milestones.note:
Covers plan M9.1–M9.3 (scripts/gtfs/check-feed.ts, the package.json gtfs:refresh script, and determinism of build.ts --force on the real county feed); m2c's build/verify-db/report/manifest must already be done. The plan's M9.1 V cannot tell an always-0 check from a real one, so the card goes further and requires scripts/gtfs/__tests__/check-feed.test.ts. It is a node:test suite that runs against a local node:http createServer and never the county host. It must have passing tests whose names contain "unchanged", "changed" (in a name without "unchanged") and "error", with no skips; a server or network failure must exit with neither 0 nor 10. On the real feed, check-feed must be read-only: assets/db and git status stay identical. It must also exit exactly 0 right after gtfs:refresh, so "changed" should mean the zip's sha256 differs from the one the committed DB was built from, not just a new ETag string (I did not check whether the county server's ETag flaps). gtfs:refresh must be one package.json && chain in the order build -> verify-db -> report, with no ; | || or lone &, and its output must show BUILT|UNCHANGED plus the report's GREEN/ORANGE rows. For M9.3: the manifest must hold no build timestamp or other non-deterministic field; schedule.db and manifest.json must be tracked and committed clean with no temp leftovers, because `git diff assets/db` exits 128 when the path is missing and passes trivially on untracked files. If the county republishes, the refresh rebuilds and gates 12/13 fail until the refreshed DB is committed; m2c's hard-coded rail end date of 20261122 is expected to go red too (M9.6). Gates 5, 8, 9 and 11 call the public county feed, which needs no key.

GATE NAMING (from the gate fix pass): Gates 4-6 match each test's FULL node:test name (suite plus leaf, case-insensitive). The describe/suite name therefore must not contain 'changed', 'unchanged' or 'error'. Name the leaves along the lines of 'unchanged feed exits 0', 'changed feed exits 10' and 'server error exits neither 0 nor 10', with at least 3 real tests. check-feed must make its HTTP calls with Node's built-in fetch or node:http(s), not curl or a library that ignores NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY, because gate 7 forces the offline error branch through a dead env proxy. Any failure must exit with a code other than 0 or 10, and check-feed must never write assets/db. For gate 11 to pass, manifest.json must not contain wall-clock fields such as builtAt (the --force rebuild has to be byte-identical), and any DB that gtfs:refresh rebuilds must be committed before the gate runs.

Shared helpers: scripts/ratchet/lib.sh — nodetest_case matches the FULL test name (describe … leaf, case-insensitive), counts only real passing leaves (not parent test() wrappers, not the Node 26 empty-file wrapper) and forbids skip/todo; jest runs via node_modules/.bin only.
